# RFC-001: Real-Time Communication Protocol Selection

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2025-01-31
**Author:** [Author Name]

---

## Summary

This document records the decision to use WebSockets as the real-time communication protocol for this project.

---

## Motivation

The project requires real-time updates, which ruled out traditional request-response patterns. A dedicated protocol was needed to handle live data efficiently.

---

## Alternatives Considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Polling | Simple to implement | Resource intensive, inefficient | Rejected |
| Server-Sent Events | Good browser support, simple | Unidirectional only | Rejected (noted as fallback) |
| gRPC Streams | High performance, typed | Additional dependency overhead | Rejected for now |
| **WebSockets** | **Bidirectional, performant, widely supported** | **Requires persistent connection management** | **Accepted** |

---

## Decision

**WebSockets** will be used for all real-time communication in this project.

## Rationale

WebSockets provide the best balance of performance and implementation simplicity among the evaluated options. The bidirectional capability offers flexibility beyond the current requirements.

---

## Implications

- [ ] WebSocket server infrastructure must be provisioned
- [ ] Connection lifecycle management must be implemented
- [ ] SSE should be documented as a fallback for restricted environments
- [ ] gRPC streams remain a future consideration if dependency overhead becomes acceptable

---

## Notes

A few things worth flagging that weren't in your original notes:

- **I added a cons column** for WebSockets since every option has tradeoffs, and honest RFC documentation is more credible
- **The implications section** is mostly placeholders since you didn't mention those details - fill those in or remove them
- **The RFC number** (RFC-001) is a placeholder, adjust to your numbering scheme
- **gRPC** is marked "rejected for now" rather than simply rejected, since your notes suggested it's a timing decision rather than a permanent rejection
